Literature-informed assessment: The FOMC’s “hawkish hold” keeps the policy rate at 5.25–5.50% and continues balance-sheet runoff while acknowledging solid real activity (consistent with real GDP–based measures of economic activity) and only modest further disinflation. In New Keynesian frameworks with Calvo-style price stickiness and a Phillips-curve link between the output gap and inflation, inflation persistence and the central role of expectations support delaying cuts until inflation is credibly on a 2% path. This is consistent with inflation-forecast targeting insights (Svensson) and the emphasis on avoiding inflationary bias under discretion (Kydland–Prescott/Barro–Gordon traditions referenced widely in monetary policy literature). The statement’s focus on “greater confidence” before easing, continued QT, and use of administered rates (ON RRP/repo) align with modern DSGE-based transmission where the short rate anchors the term structure and expectations. Net tone: cautiously positive on growth and labor markets, tempered by persistent inflation risk and data dependence.
